projects.title: Distributed RLHF Training Infrastructure
projects.summary: A scaled-down but architecturally realistic RLHF training stack: a distributed actor-learner pipeline (rollout generation + reward scoring + policy update) for a small open-source LLM, optimized for throughput and hardened for reliability, with a clean researcher-facing interface. This is the most direct simulation of the actual job — building and operating the critical infra researchers depend on.

components.name: Distributed actor-learner RLHF pipeline
components.description: A multi-GPU/multi-node RLHF training loop (e.g. using Ray or torchrun + FSDP/DeepSpeed) that separates rollout generation from policy/value updates, implemented from the ground up rather than calling a single high-level library function, for a small-to-mid-size open model.
components.rationale: Building the distributed training/inference split by hand demonstrates both the algorithmic (RLHF) and large-scale distributed-systems experience the listing asks for directly.

components.name: Throughput profiling and optimization pass
components.description: Systematic profiling of the pipeline (GPU utilization, rollout generation latency, communication overhead) followed by concrete optimizations such as batched/efficient inference for rollouts, mixed precision, gradient checkpointing, or overlapping compute and communication, with before/after benchmarks.
components.rationale: Measured, documented speedups on a real bottleneck is direct evidence of the 'obsessive' performance focus the role names as its core mandate.

components.name: Fault tolerance and monitoring layer
components.description: Checkpointing, automatic restart-on-failure, and a monitoring dashboard (loss/reward/KL curves, worker health) so the pipeline can run unattended and recover from node or process failures.
components.rationale: Demonstrating that the system survives failures and reports its own health is concrete evidence it could be depended on by a researcher who isn't the author.

components.name: Researcher-facing config API and docs
components.description: A simple, well-documented configuration interface (YAML/CLI) plus example run scripts and a short design doc, written so a hypothetical ML researcher with no knowledge of the internals could launch and interpret a training run.
components.rationale: A usable, documented interface aimed at a non-infra audience is the clearest solo-project proxy for the collaborative, researcher-enabling work the role emphasizes.

roadmap.milestone: Working single-node RLHF loop for a small model
Scale the loop to a distributed multi-process/multi-GPU actor-learner setup
Profile and optimize throughput with documented benchmarks
Add checkpointing, restart, and monitoring for unattended reliability
Ship a documented researcher-facing config/CLI layer

projects.title: RLHF Algorithm Zoo and Robustness Benchmark
projects.summary: An algorithm-implementation-focused project: build reward modeling and multiple finetuning algorithms (PPO, DPO, RLOO or similar) from scratch behind a common interface, then deliberately stress-test them for known RLHF failure modes (reward hacking, KL blowups, instability) and publish a reproducible benchmark. This emphasizes deep algorithmic fluency and the 'improve the algorithms' half of the job.

components.name: Reward model + PPO baseline from scratch
components.description: A from-scratch (not just library-call) implementation of reward model training and PPO-based RLHF fine-tuning on a small open model and public preference dataset.
components.rationale: Implementing PPO/RLHF at the algorithm level is the most literal evidence of the listed 'implementing LLM finetuning algorithms' experience.

components.name: Pluggable alternative finetuning algorithms
components.description: Additional algorithms (e.g. DPO, RLOO) implemented behind a shared trainer interface so they can be swapped in and compared against the PPO baseline with minimal code changes.
components.rationale: A maintainable, extensible algorithm suite mirrors the ongoing 'build, maintain, and improve algorithms' responsibility rather than a one-off script.

components.name: Failure-mode stress test suite
components.description: A set of deliberately adversarial or edge-case training configurations (aggressive learning rates, weak KL penalties, reward-hacking-prone reward models) used to surface and then fix instability in each algorithm implementation.
components.rationale: Actively hunting for and fixing instability is direct evidence of the robustness focus the listing calls out as central to the role.

components.name: Reproducible cross-algorithm benchmark report
components.description: An experiment-tracked (e.g. via Weights & Biases) comparison of the algorithms on sample efficiency, wall-clock speed, and stability, written up with plots and a short analysis of trade-offs.
components.rationale: A rigorous, reproducible comparison shows the same performance-and-robustness rigor described in the listing, applied at the algorithm rather than systems layer.

roadmap.milestone: Reward model and PPO baseline working end-to-end
Add DPO/RLOO behind a common trainer interface
Build and run the failure-mode stress test suite, fixing discovered issues
Publish the reproducible cross-algorithm benchmark report

projects.title: RLHF Training Observability and Developer Productivity Toolkit
projects.summary: A tooling-and-usability-focused project built on top of an existing open-source RLHF library (e.g. TRL/trlx): an observability dashboard, an automated diagnostics tool for common RLHF failure signatures, and a documentation/onboarding kit aimed at a non-infra researcher. This emphasizes the 'make other people more productive' and cross-functional collaboration angle of the role rather than raw systems throughput.

components.name: Training observability dashboard
components.description: A metrics dashboard layered on an existing RLHF pipeline that surfaces reward, KL divergence, and sample generations in real time during training runs.
components.rationale: Visibility into training health is a concrete ease-of-use and progress-enabling improvement over a bare training script.

components.name: Automated failure-signature diagnostics
components.description: A checker that watches training metrics for known RLHF pathologies (reward collapse, KL explosion, degenerate/repetitive outputs) and surfaces likely root causes with actionable hints.
components.rationale: Automating diagnosis of recurring failure modes is direct evidence of improving robustness and reducing time researchers spend firefighting.

components.name: Researcher quickstart kit
components.description: A short onboarding guide, example configs, and a thin CLI wrapper that let someone unfamiliar with the codebase launch and interpret a training run without reading the internals.
components.rationale: Writing for a reader who isn't the author is the closest solo-project proxy for enabling researchers who depend on, but don't build, the infrastructure.

components.name: Design walkthrough and contribution guide
components.description: A written (or recorded) deep-dive explaining the toolkit's internals and design trade-offs, plus a guide for how a teammate could extend it, structured as if handing the project off to a collaborator.
components.rationale: Explicitly writing to enable a hypothetical collaborator to extend the work demonstrates the pairing/collaboration mindset the listing values, in the closest form a solo project allows.

roadmap.milestone: Integrate with an existing RLHF library and ship the metrics dashboard
Write the researcher quickstart kit and CLI wrapper
Produce the design walkthrough and contribution guide
